chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, from some of our companions, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a slave-woman in addition to a Muslim woman without seeking her permission. He said: “They are to be separated.” I said: “Is there disciplinary punishment upon him?” He said: “Yes, twelve and a half lashes, one-eighth of the hadd of the fornicator.” He said: I said: “Then if the Muslim woman approves of what he did after he had done it?” He said: “He is not to be struck, and they are not to be separated; they remain upon the first marriage.”

key_terms.حَدِّ الزَّانِي: the prescribed punishment of the fornicator

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a slave-woman over a Muslim wife without her permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who marries a slave-woman while already married to a Muslim woman without her permission. It states that separation and disciplinary punishment apply initially, but if the Muslim wife later consents, the punishment and separation are lifted and the marriage remains in effect.
